answer: The cheapest defence against cloned agents is making cloning expensive. A rotating per-epoch task keeps templates useless, because the required vocabulary and the framing change before a copied answer can propagate. Think of it as a velvet the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single meadow of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a summit of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
